---
title: Getting started
---

## Get the materials

Choose a week in the sidebar. Download the **complete lab folder** and extract it before opening a notebook. This keeps supporting Python modules alongside the notebook.

You can also clone the whole course repository:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/YaolangZhong/U_Tokyo_Comp_Econ_Course.git
cd U_Tokyo_Comp_Econ_Course
```

## Set up Python

Use Python 3 and a separate environment for your coursework:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
# macOS / Linux
source .venv/bin/activate
# Windows PowerShell: .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install jupyterlab numpy scipy matplotlib
```

These packages provide a starting environment, not a verified dependency lock for every lab. Later notebooks may require additional libraries, including PyTorch; consult their import cells. Lab environments will be refined as each week's content is updated.

## Run a lab

From the repository root, for example:

```bash
cd weeks/week_09/lab
python -m jupyterlab
```

Open the notebook in JupyterLab and run its cells in order. Keep the notebook's working directory set to its lab folder so local Python imports resolve.

## Read online or run locally

The website displays the notebook's saved code and results. Reading a lab online does not execute Python. Download the lab to change parameters or reproduce the calculations yourself.

For an introduction to Python, see @quantecon-python and @coding-economists.
